questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Learning a new language, acedemic challenge to study abroad and the reputation of the city and university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, as both KI and KU had good webpages/ and send almost all necessary  information by email prior to the exchange

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The international coordinators were very present and nice in the first week!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Single room, sharing apartment (two people), sharing apartment (four people) and dorm rooms.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Fully equipt kitchens either common or in the apartments. All you needed was there!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You have to be prepared to be social :)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was quit a bit emailen back a n forth with forms that neede to be signed both by my home university and the host university. But It worked out in the end.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Not sure what part of it was exactly the "registration process". But you could say that it was devided in the correspondance with the internation coordinator by email prior to the arrivel and then the registration and start at the host university which included getting id-cards, inctructions about the course etc.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international coordinators, global friends and the teachers on the course.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Besides my misunderstanding which hospital the course/clinical placement would be on it went smooth.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Specify clearly if you wish to do the rotations at specific hospitalts.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the course corresponded to the level of the courses in the last part of the MA in medicin in UCPH. Maybe a bit higher than UCHP

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was more "old school". I felt treated a bit like a child sometimes. Like they didnt trust our own responsibility to learn the curriculum. They were very nice but the expectations were high, and you where expected to be able to answer when pointed out in class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Clinical Medicine - Emphasis on Reproduction and Development. (Pediatrics, gynecology, obstetrics and clinical genetics)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Especially the pediatrics part was very very well done!

questions.answer: The general costs of living were higher than expected.

questions.answer: Especially groceries were more expensive than in DK!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Spent quit some time in the gym and on the badminton courts the campus offered.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Badminton and the student union house.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Södermalm, Djurgården and the archipelago.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quit easy as danish and swedish people a quit similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The swedish people are very polite and correct. You might experience difficulties if you challenge that to much.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their food, culture for fika (coffee breaks), language and academic ambitions.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
They are very nice but ambitious, and that is a good thing! 
Participate in the social offers the university have. 
Ask if you are in doubt, people are very willing to help!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use the student union and international coordinators! They are there for you.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning the language and how I have grown academically.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting to know the swedish students properly and managing the course while also being social and enjoying the exchange.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
